CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hypogonadism follow-up; testosterone replacement therapy management.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Paul Edwards is a 64-year-old HIV-positive male presenting for follow-up of hypogonadism. Patient reports feeling well on current testosterone replacement therapy at 1 mL every 10 days. He notes improved vigor, better sleep, and positive changes in bloodwork since initiation of testosterone. Patient reports taking finasteride 5 mg at half-pill dosing and cialis variably (5 mg on workout days, 2.5 mg otherwise), though he states he has been out of cialis recently. Patient is interested in discussing potential dose increase from 140 mg to 175 mg but denies recent weight gain or muscle mass changes. He is pleased with recent improvements in cholesterol and triglyceride levels, noting triglycerides decreased from 265 mg/dL to 145 mg/dL since starting testosterone replacement in May 2026.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports sleeping well and feeling vigorous. No acute complaints. Denies physical changes despite feeling good systemically.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
HIV infection
Hypogonadism
Hyperlipidemia (history of elevated triglycerides)

MEDICATIONS
Testosterone injection 1 mL every 10 days
Finasteride 5 mg one-half tablet daily
Cialis 2.5-5 mg daily as needed

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works out regularly. Uses Walmart pharmacy for medications. Denies recent lifestyle changes.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient appears trim in appearance. Cardiovascular: Heart sounds normal, no concerns. Pulmonary: Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally.

RESULTS
PSA: 0.6 ng/mL (previously 0.5 last year; normal <4 ng/mL)
Testosterone: Previously >1,500 ng/dL at peak; current level approximately 700 ng/dL (on day 8 of injection cycle)
Red blood cell count: Increased but stable
Cholesterol and triglycerides: Significantly improved; triglycerides decreased from 265 mg/dL to 145 mg/dL over 5 months
Estradiol: Not elevated

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
64-year-old HIV-positive male with hypogonadism on testosterone replacement therapy doing well clinically and biochemically. Patient requests dose increase to 175 mg; however, current testosterone levels already reaching peaks >1,500 ng/dL, which increases risk of polycythemia and cardiovascular complications. Will maintain current dose at 140 mg given excellent clinical response, stable PSA, normal estradiol, and improved lipid profile. Advised against dose escalation due to risk stratification. Patient counseled on dangers of excessive testosterone dosing. PSA monitoring to continue annually. Consider estradiol testing in fall if needed. Refill prescriptions: testosterone, finasteride, and cialis as paper prescriptions per patient preference at Walmart pharmacy.
